sections.h2: Suffolk's size and what it means for a seller
sections.html:
No Virginia city has more land than Suffolk, which sits in southeastern Virginia's Hampton Roads area. Of 428.91 square miles, 399.17 are land and 29.74 are water. The size dates to 1974, when the original city merged with the former Nansemond County, the city of Nansemond, and the towns of Holland and Whaleyville, all under Suffolk's name. Residents numbered 94,324 in 2020 and an estimated 104,699 in 2025.

Farmland, a piece of the Great Dismal Swamp, small villages and a suburban north end all lie within the limits, so two Suffolk houses can have little in common. The 2020 census recorded 38,364 housing units, with 7.3 percent unoccupied, and 27.1 percent of residents lived in rural areas.

Politically the city has seven boroughs: Chuckatuck, Cypress, Holy Neck, Nansemond, Sleepy Hole, Suffolk and Whaleyville. Whaleyville, Holy Neck and Chuckatuck lean rural. Nansemond, Suffolk, Sleepy Hole and Cypress lean urban.

Tell buyers which borough the property is in, because that hints at lot size, road type and surroundings. The Driver Historic District and the Suffolk Historic District also exist, so an older house deserves a question to the city about any historic overlay before exterior changes.

Summers are hot and sticky, winters mild to cool. Rain totals 51.82 inches in an average year over about 123.7 days, and snow adds roughly 5.8 inches.

With wet weather on roughly a third of days and swamp-edged land, inspectors look at gutters, crawl spaces, drainage and air conditioning. Cleaning and servicing those before you sell can shorten the repair request list.

The city took over its own road system on July 1, 2006, which means road and ditch questions near your house go to Suffolk and not the state.

Expect questions about reaching the rest of the region. Highways include U.S. 13, 17, 58, 258 and 460, plus State Route 10. Interstate 664 touches the northeastern corner on the Beltway, and the Monitor-Merrimac Memorial Bridge-Tunnel goes to Newport News. Local buses come from Suffolk Transit, which has two links to Hampton Roads Transit. Three freight railroads run through.

North Suffolk and the rural south feel like different places on a commute, so give a drive time from the actual address. A buyer who works near the Beltway cares about the northern edge. One who works on a farm cares about the roads to the south, and the city's road system is where questions about a ditch or a bridge approach go.

sections.h2: What is the Suffolk real estate tax rate?
sections.html:
Suffolk charges $1.06 per $100 of assessed value citywide, with higher rates in two special districts. These rates run through June 30, 2027.

AreaRate per $100 of assessed value
Citywide$1.06
Downtown Business District$1.165
Route 17 Taxing District$1.30

Bills come due in two installments, December 5 and June 5; a weekend or holiday pushes the date to the next business day. Find out whether your address is in a special district before estimating what you owe.

Pay or ask questions in person at either Treasurer office: downtown at 442 West Washington Street or in North Suffolk at 2000 Bennetts Creek Park Road. Hours are 8:30 a.m. to 5 p.m. on weekdays, and the number is 757-514-4275.

Every parcel is listed and valued by the City Assessor's Office, 442 W. Washington Street, 757-514-7475. Only the owner of record can get proposed assessment property record cards.

  • Social Services oversees tax relief for seniors, disabled citizens and disabled former service members.
  • A rehabilitation abatement gives a partial exemption for qualifying renovation or replacement of structures in maturing neighborhoods.
  • Farm, horticultural and forest acreage in the land use program is valued for what it is used for, not what it might sell for.

A value you dispute can go to the Board of Equalization under state law. There the owner must overcome the assumption that the assessor is correct. Your rights and deadlines are laid out on the Assessment Process page of the city site, which is worth reading before you file.

Two city offices handle different jobs, and calling the wrong one wastes a day. The Assessor decides what your property is worth and holds the record cards, so valuation questions, disputes and land use or rehabilitation program questions start at 757-514-7475. The Treasurer sends the bill and takes the payment, so due dates, balances, payment plans and payoff figures go to 757-514-4275.

Relief for seniors and disabled owners runs through Social Services, which is a third door altogether. If you are selling a house where a relative received relief, ask whether any of it affects the final bill.

At a sale the city's tax lien gets paid first from the price, and the Treasurer lifts it after payment. Whoever closes the sale must direct proceeds to the tax, penalties and interest included.

  • Virginia's grantor tax is 50 cents per $500 and falls on the seller unless the contract moves it.
  • This year's tax is divided as the contract says.
  • Courts can order the sale of delinquent land after a waiting period, following 30 days' notice from the city.
  • A payment plan reaching 72 months is possible with the treasurer's agreement.

Ask the Treasurer for a written payoff just before closing and pass it to the closing agent with any mortgage payoff.

Closing goes better when these items are handled the week before.

  1. Phone the Treasurer for the balance as of closing day, with any penalty and interest.
  2. Verify which installments, December 5 or June 5, are already paid.
  3. Check whether the address lies in the Downtown Business District or the Route 17 Taxing District, because the rate differs there.
  4. Settle in the contract how this year's tax is split.
  5. Have the deed details ready so the price appears on page one, and budget for the grantor tax.

If the bill is behind and a court sale worries you, the Treasurer is your first call.

sections.h2: Selling a Suffolk house for cash
sections.html:
No lender means nothing rides on a loan approval or appraisal. That suits a house needing repairs, rural acreage that is hard to finance, or an inherited property with tax owed. The buyer evaluates the home as is and submits a written offer.

Before calling, round up the newest tax bill, a mortgage statement if you owe on the house, and paperwork for any land use or rehabilitation program on the parcel. Land in the program follows special rules, so ask the Assessor what a sale does to it. Then put the offer next to a standard listing and pick whichever suits your timeline. At closing, taxes, any mortgage and the grantor tax come out of the proceeds.

faqs.q: What is Suffolk's real estate tax rate?
faqs.a: $1.06 per $100 citywide. Two special districts pay more: $1.165 downtown and $1.30 in the Route 17 Taxing District. The listed rates run through June 30, 2027.

faqs.q: When is Suffolk property tax due?
faqs.a: Half is due December 5 and half June 5. If either falls on a weekend or holiday, you have until the next business day.

faqs.q: Who do I call about a Suffolk assessment?
faqs.a: Call the City Assessor's Office at 757-514-7475 or visit 442 W. Washington Street. Only the owner of record gets proposed assessment record cards.

faqs.q: Is Suffolk the largest city in Virginia?
faqs.a: Yes, by land, at about 399 square miles. Its population was 94,324 in 2020.

faqs.q: Does Suffolk have a program for farm or forest land?
faqs.a: Yes, a land use program bases the tax on how agricultural, horticultural or forest land is used. The assessor can tell you whether you qualify.
